title: Basic adverbs, adjective-adverbs, and position
goal: Recognize common adverbs, use adjectives as adverbs, and place both naturally in simple Norwegian clauses.

objectives.statement: Recognize common adverbs, use adjectives as adverbs, and place both naturally in simple Norwegian clauses.

spans.value: Anna and Erik are preparing food before some friends arrive. Nora is sleeping in the next room.
Ja, jeg kommer ofte sent, men jeg er ikke sen i dag.

blocks.translation: Yes, I often arrive late, but I’m not late today.

spans.value: Bra. Jeg arbeider langsomt i dag.
Jeg kan hjelpe. Jeg kutter grønnsakene raskt.

blocks.translation: I can help. I’ll cut the vegetables quickly.

spans.value: Takk. Legg glassene forsiktig på bordet.

blocks.translation: Thanks. Put the glasses carefully on the table.
All right. Am I speaking too loudly?

spans.value: Ja, du snakker litt høyt. Nora sover.

blocks.translation: Yes, you’re speaking a little loudly. Nora is sleeping.

spans.value: Flott. Du hjelper alltid når vi har fest.

blocks.translation: Great. You always help when we have a party.

A common English-influenced mistake is to put the adverb before the verb:

A place expression can follow the manner adverb:

sections.title: Transfer: helping at a school event

spans.value: Imagine a changed everyday situation. Mina and Jonas are arranging chairs and preparing drinks before a school event. The vocabulary changes, but the grammar job stays the same.

no.value: Mina er rolig, og hun arbeider rolig.

en.value: Mina is calm, and she works calmly.

spans.value: The final pair shows why meaning matters even when the form looks identical. The first
describes Mina. The second describes how she works.
